3e6f48599a1e: Yes, and for scheduling it is the stronger one: multi-date picking, capacity and conflict checks, public booking pages and Screen Flow outputs are built in, alongside five calendar views. CalendarAnything adds Gantt and Kanban layouts and calendar sync, which matter only if browsing is the whole job.
9258a8ccc7fb: How much does CalendarAnything cost compared with MultiDatePick?
ca1aeff854b0: Silverline's FAQ lists CalendarAnything at $199 per user per year with a minimum of 10 licenses. MultiDatePick is $20 per user per month, one plan with every feature included, and a 30-day free trial with no card.
1c1dcf527d87: Does MultiDatePick sync with Outlook or Google Calendar?
ac4f88d088cf: It offers an Add to Calendar file after each save, which opens in Outlook, Google Calendar and Apple Calendar. It does not keep a two-way sync.
45ca6a8a06b6: Can MultiDatePick show records from any object?
8d3fc4e9f779: Yes. Any standard or custom object with a Date or Date/Time field, including Task and Event, and records reached through up to five lookups with the Rollup Field.
0b759468a98d: CalendarAnything puts Salesforce records on calendars to look at. MultiDatePick shows them too, and lets people pick dates, book time and save records with the rules enforced. For scheduling work in Salesforce, MultiDatePick is the better choice.
33b5cbc7c903: If you search for a Salesforce calendar app, CalendarAnything comes up early. It has been on the AppExchange for years, and it is good at what it was built for: putting many kinds of Salesforce records on shared calendars that teams browse, filter and print. MultiDatePick starts from the other end: the moment someone picks dates or books a time, and the records that come out of it.
340f1ad741f0: Both are native, both work with standard and custom objects, and both are configured without code. But a calendar you can only look at leaves the real work to someone else: booking without double booking, picking many dates at once, letting customers schedule themselves. <t1>That is where MultiDatePick pulls ahead.</t1>
5a26ba727b1e: CalendarAnything details come from Silverline's own product and FAQ pages as of November 2026. Check their site for the latest.
